title: CLAY CITY SCHOOL BOARD MEETS
full_story:
The Clay City School Board met Thursday evening and worked through a very busy agenda and tackled a few thorny issues and acted on numerous personnel issues.

Board Chairman Misty Lindeman called the meeting to order and with no visitor present to address the board they quickly dove into action by approving the meeting agenda and past meeting minutes.

Superintendent John Neubaum went over the Financial Report and noted as the school year draws to a close, finances are pretty much tracking as they should and there was nothing exceptional to report.  The board approved the report unanimously.  Chairman Sue Lindeman questioned the money being spent on food purchases that seems disproportionate to what is needed.  Supt. Neubaum said they are getting the funds from the federal government, and it must be spent on food.  Lindeman then wondered aloud whether the money could not be used for other cafeteria/kitchen related expenses rather than on food alone.  Neubaum said he would look into the matter.

As Supt. Neubaum moved into informational items he updated the board on enrollment and then talked about the best interest determination meeting with DCFS about foster children attending Clay City Schools.  He said children in the Xenia area were considered for attendance at Clay City rather than Flora but providing bus transportation was not feasible.  An offer was made by the district, but DCFS never followed up.  Now the government entity is considering requiring the district to pay past mileage reimbursement.  Neubaum shifted gears and presented a PowerPoint presentation about Spring Data about student performance this spring.  The slides showed previous results for reading and math that revealed large segments of elementary students were either one grade level behind or two.  Using the concept of Multi-Tiered System of Supports or MTSS, district teachers used techniques that have been shown to offer encouraging results in moving students to a better place in their learning process and demonstrated exceptional growth in both reading and math.  While he said some questioned whether students are performing better, he said the data collected demonstrates significant improvement is being made as students and teachers are more focused on learning.  Strides are also being made in professional development, and they will continue incorporation of MTSS in the SIP (School Improvement Plan) to help students achieve mastery of the subjects and get back to performing at their grade level.  Supt. Neubaum then provided an update on the continuing issue of FOIA or Freedom of Information Act requests.  The issue is that certain attorneys are requesting large quantities of school district information and have launched a website posting information that at the very least is misleading.  Neubaum cautioned board members and the public to be wary of raw data that the so-called public interest groups are presenting on various websites once they collect information from various school districts.  He says they often present information that is wrong or misleading or they come to conclusions based on bad or incomplete information and present it as fact.  Districts across Illinois and the country are continually subjected to these FOIA requests and there doesn’t appear to be an end in sight.

Principal Brian Wattles presented his report and went over a long list of student and class achievements.  Topics covered included Pre-K End of Year Celebration, Kindergarten Preview Day, Math Night, Elementary America 250 Program with students getting energized about the upcoming milestone for our country, P.E. Fun Day, 5th grade D.A.R.E. graduation, 8th grade students passed their Illinois Constitution test, a variety of field trips have wrapped up including a trip to the Candles Holocaust Museum in Terre Haute for 6th grade students as well as taking in an Evansville Otters baseball game, and there was a jr. high bowling trip to Salem.  At Clay City High School, students completed I-Ready and ACT Testing, there was the FFA Awards Banquet and Jr. high and high school awards, spring band concert and the band trip to Holiday World.  In student achievement, Jackson Dye and Taylee Grey were accepted into the Clay County CEO Program for the upcoming school year.  Finley Flexter, Hadley Mitchell, Avery Henderson, Jacelyn Thompson and Delany Martin competed in the SIJHSAA State Track Meet, the 4 x 100 Relay Tam placed in the top 8 and brought home medals and district athletes continued competing for the North Clay/Clay City Co-op in baseball, softball and track. The Bass Fishing Team participated in the Newton Regional, and the sports awards banquet was held celebrating accomplishments this year.  National Honor Society visited the University of Illinois and Bus Driver and Teacher Appreciation Week took place.

Next, the board accepted resignations from Paraprofessional Haylee James, School Counselor Sydney Hall, Science Teacher Marshall Brummer and High School Cross Country Coach Courtney Mitchell.  Employment was offered to Richelle Britton Yates as Early Childhood Educator, Grace Horton as School Counselor and Luke Allen as High School English/Language Arts Teacher.

The board discussed a proposed contract for a School Resource Officer (SRO) through the Clay County Sheriff’s Office.  Sheriff Andy Myers was on hand to answer questions from the board.  The salary figure cited was $75,600 and members began questioning whether the expense was necessary for the three-year proposal.  Myers and the board respectfully sparred over the duties of the assigned deputy between the school district, the village of Clay City and other assigned duties in the county.  The Sheriff said he understood members’ concern and whatever action they take he would work with them to come to an agreement over how to proceed, with pros and cons for either option.  Board Member Oliver Bangert questioned whether they could justify the expense at a time when district enrollment is shrinking.  Misty Lindeman stated that if needed other positions could be eliminated, because she didn’t want to have to explain to parents why an SRO wasn’t on hand should a tragedy ever occur.  Sheriff Myers stated that if the district needs to reconsider the agreement after a year, he would work with them about that as well, but he needs to make plans about hiring for the near future, and their decision would have a bearing on that.  In the end, a motion was made to approve the three-year agreement.  The measure passed on a 4-2 vote with Misty Lindeman, Erin Boyd, Dusty Thompson and Mary Joe Workman voting Yes and Oliver Bangert and Mary Joe Patridge voting No.

In other action, the board approved a measure to rent a classroom to SESE (South Eastern Special Education) for Autism I.  They also approved renewing membership in the Illinois High School Association and approved the school board meeting dates for the new school year (to remain on the third Thursday of each month).  The board also approved the Consolidated District Plan and approved the Tentative FY26-27 Budget Amendment and set a public hearing for 5:45pm on June 25.  They also voted to change the date for the June meeting to June 25 at 6:00pm.

The board then voted to go into closed session.  When they returned to open session, they voted to uphold student discipline as presented and approved Non-Certified Salaries for 2026-2027 and then adjourned.

title: JOHNSONVILLE MAN ARRESTED
full_story:
A Johnsonville man was arrested by Wayne County deputies Tuesday evening on a warrant having four charges from Jasper County.

Deputies arrested Robert E. Reid on alleged charges including aggravated domestic battery-strangulation, public aggravated battery, domestic battery, and criminal damage to property.

Reports state Reid was visiting The Hill Bar in Jasper County and allegedly punched a female victim in the back of her head and continue to allege intentional strangulation.  The property damage was the victim’s cell phone.  Charges were filed on May 17th.

Deputies moved Reid to the Wayne County Jail where he was booked.  He is being held for his extradition to Jasper County to answer the alleged charges.

title: NORTH WAYNE BOARD MEETING
full_story:
The North Wayne School Board met in regular session Wednesday night.

The board approved the registration dates for the next school year, with online registration from August 3rd through 11th, and in-person registration available on August 10th and 11th, overnight trips for FFA to attend an Officer’s Retreat and the State Convention, and purchasing “Big Ideas Math” as the new K-8 math curriculum on a three-year contract.

In personnel matters the board hired Collin Klingler as Athletic Director, Tyson Lowe as Assistant Athletic Director, Paul Lowe and Katlyn Tannahill as aides at Mt. Erie Elementary, and Kristen Duvall as Cisne Middle School Assistant Softball Coach.

They also accepted a letter of retirement from Troy Helm, effective May 29th, FMLA leave for two employees, and personal leave days and dock days requests.

title: ROTARY PICKLEBALL
full_story:
The Flora Rotary Club is sponsoring its 1st Annual Pickleball Tournament the weekend of June 19th and 20th at the Rotary Pickleball Courts.

On June 19th from 5 to 6:45 pm Senior’s age 55 and up will play and from 6:45 to 8:30 pm those 18 and under will play.  Then on Saturday from 8 to 9:45 am men’s doubles intermediates will play, from 9:45 to 11:30 am Men’s doubles advanced will play.  Women’s doubles intermediate will play from 11:30 to 1:15 pm, With women’s doubles advanced will play from 1:15 to 3 pm.  Mixed doubles intermediate will take the courts from 3 to 4:45 pm, and mixed doubles advanced will play from 4:45 to 6:30 pm.

Entry fee is $30 per person and sign up is available through a QR code on event flyers and more information is available on the Flora Rotary Facebook page.  Each team is guaranteed 5 games.  There is a maximum of 12 teams per division so sign up soon.  Registration deadline is June 12th.  Division winners will receive their entry fee back.

title: EMERGENCY REPAIRS TO I64 BRIDGE
full_story:
All lanes of the Interstate 64 bridge over the Wabash River near Grayville will be closed for emergency repairs next week.

Officials with the Illinois Department of Transportation say the closure will take place from 7 pm to 7 am on Tuesday, May 26th and Wednesday May 27th.  In the event of bad weather, repairs will be rescheduled for the nights of May 27th and 28th.

Posted detours will direct eastbound traffic via Ill. Route 130 and Illinois Route 1 and westbound traffic via the Indiana 65 exit at milepost 18.

This is the second time emergency repairs have been made to the bridge.

title: MEMORIAL DAY GAS PRICES
full_story:
Prices at the pump remain at record levels across Illinois as many fuel up their cars for one of the busiest travel days of the year.

As the war in Iran lingers on, Patrick DeHaan, the Head of Petroleum Analysis at GasBuddy, reports prices will remain at record levels as long as the Strait of Hormuz remains closed.

Last week, Illinois set a record for diesel prices, with the average price above six dollars a gallon.

While the US continues to tap the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, DeHaan reports, the level in reserves is now under 375 million barrels.
